title: Apply late and corrected records so load order never changes the result
problem: Real sources send corrections, and files arrive late or out of order. If the latest file loaded wins, the final table depends on arrival order, and a rerun after an outage produces different data from the original run. Nobody notices until two reports disagree.
context: Builds on idempotent, atomic loads. Records now carry the time the source changed them, and a key can appear again in a later batch with new values.
impact: Determinism is what makes a rebuild a valid repair. Without it, every rerun is a new, unexplained version of the truth.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The design states which version of a record wins, using the record's own change time rather than load order, and how ties are broken deterministically.
An older version arriving after a newer one is counted as superseded, not loaded, and the reconciliation still adds up.
Loading the same set of batches in every order the test chooses produces identical final tables, compared with a SQL query.
The table can be rebuilt from the retained batch files into a fresh database, producing the same contents.
Automated tests cover a correction, a late older version, a tie, and at least two load orders. All pass at the submitted revision.
The learner explains the winning rule, one rejected alternative such as last-loaded-wins, and a source behavior that would still break determinism.

constraints: Standard library, including sqlite3 and csv, plus a test runner only. No ORM, dataframe or validation library.
Keep history out of scope unless the design justifies it. The table holds the current version of each record.
Do not push to a remote or open a pull request as part of this task.

scope.description: Record version semantics and replay determinism.

investigation_areas: What event time and arrival time each mean for this data, and which one the source can be trusted for
How a SQL upsert can express the winning rule, and where it cannot
How to test order independence without enumerating every permutation
testing_expectations: Run the project's own test suite. State the exact command in the design.
documentation_requirements: Record the winning rule, the tie break and the rejected alternative in the learner design.
